chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about a man who has a debt due at a specified term, so his creditor comes to him and says, 'Pay me such and such an amount, and I shall write off the remainder for you,' or 'Pay me part of it, and I shall extend the term for what remains upon you.'
He said: 'I do not see any problem with it, for it does not increase upon the principal of his wealth.'
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Says: 'Then you shall have your principal; neither shall you deal unjustly nor will you be dealt with unjustly.'

key_terms.لَا تَظْلِمُونَ وَلَا تُظْلَمُونَ: Neither shall you deal unjustly nor will you be dealt with unjustly

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to forgive part of a debt in exchange for immediate partial payment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that both forgiving the remainder of a debt or extending its term are permissible forms of reconciliation, as neither increases the principal capital, thereby avoiding riba. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic finance to facilitate ease for debtors while protecting the creditor's core asset, reflecting the Quranic principle of mutual non-injustice. The narration highlights the practical application of 'sulh' (reconciliation) in resolving financial obligations without incurring interest-based penalties.
